clauses.reason: Clause 1 establishes the Los Angeles-Long Beach Harbor Naval Defensive Sea Area and prescribes its control regulations. EO 9720, signed by President Truman on May 8, 1946, states that the listed areas "are hereby discontinued" and lists the Los Angeles-Long Beach Harbor Naval Defensive Sea Area, established by Executive Order No. 8953 of November 27, 1941, as item 5. EO 9720 is an express discontinuance of the area by a later order that names it and whose text is held. The regulations, the call for assistance and the Navy charge are tied by their own words to this area, so they ended with it. EO 9720 states no separate effective date; the signing date is recorded, and the Federal Register publication date was May 10, 1946.

Clause 2 states that the order supersedes Executive Order No. 8403 of May 7, 1940, which had established the same area. A supersession sentence is performed when the order issues, so the command was exhausted on the order's date, November 27, 1941; the order states no later effective date. Its result, that EO 8403 no longer operated, is an accrued effect that is not undone by the later discontinuance of the area.

inventory_overrides.reason: Separates the area-and-regulations clause from the one-time sentence superseding EO 8403.
The supersession of EO 8403 is a separate one-time command with its own date.

research_rationale:
The registered working text is the Federal Register text layer of EO 8953 (6 FR 6123, Federal Register of December 2, 1941; machine-extracted text, original page images not inspected). The order is dated November 27, 1941 and establishes the Los Angeles-Long Beach Harbor Naval Defensive Sea Area under section 44 of the Criminal Code, prescribes the regulations for vessels in it, calls on Government and local authorities to assist in enforcing them, charges the Secretary of the Navy with their publication and enforcement, and supersedes Executive Order No. 8403 of May 7, 1940. Inventory corrected into two clauses: the area and its regulations (characters 714 to 5507 of the held text) and the one-time supersession sentence (characters 5508 to 5666). Clause 1 ends by express discontinuance in EO 9720 of May 8, 1946 (11 FR 5105, Federal Register of May 10, 1946; filed May 9, 1946), whose list of areas discontinued includes the Los Angeles-Long Beach Harbor Naval Defensive Sea Area established by Executive Order No. 8953 of November 27, 1941. Clause 2 was performed when the order issued on November 27, 1941. Recorded date for the end of clause 1 is the signing date, May 8, 1946, because EO 9720 states no other effective date; publication in the Federal Register was May 10, 1946. savings.reason: State transferred_or_accrued. Neither EO 8953 nor EO 9720 contains a savings clause. The supersession of Executive Order No. 8403 of May 7, 1940 was completed when EO 8953 issued, and its result stands independently of EO 8953's later discontinuance; no held source shows any other continuing effect.
